name: Alice Blue
lede: Alice Blue is a very pale, faintly cool blue-white, named for Alice Roosevelt and now one of the CSS and X11 color keywords.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines Alice blue as a US term, named after Alice, the wife of Theodore Roosevelt [1]. The dictionary's own wording may be a slip, since the books we hold do not otherwise establish the family relation [1]. Paterson calls the shade greenish-blue, yet he also gives the screen version, AliceBlue, with the code #F0F8FF [1]. That code is nearly white with a cool tint, so the old description and the screen color are not the same thing [1].

The name is first recorded in our sources in 1912, in Ridgway's color standards, and it later appears in the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary and in ISCC-NBS of 1955 [3]. The books we have read say nothing more about its origin, so this page does not add a story that they do not support [1].

sections.title: On screen
sections.body:
AliceBlue is one of the 140 named colors of the X11 set, which web browsers adopted as CSS color keywords [1]. Among our named colors its closest neighbor in family is [[ghost-white]], and it sits at the pale end of the [[light-blue]] range [3].

Like all hex values for named colors, it is a screen approximation and will shift between displays [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 82 contain this color, 0.34% of the total, as photographed [4]. It is most often a light inside a painting, which fits a color that is nearly white [4]. The earliest match is from 1332, which is 580 years before the name's first record, so that match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph and not evidence of any pigment [4].
